entry.title: Why has the subject of transgender identity become so polarizing? And how can we deepen our understanding of the issue? Simon Coutu’s Transpositions, the latest installment of NFB YouTube-based documentary initiative ON FILME, launches
entry.summary: Transpositions by documentary filmmaker Simon Coutu is now streaming on YouTube. This highly topical work explores the rise of transphobia and the weaponization of trans identity in Quebec’s political and media discourse.

entry.title: Government of Canada supports women farmers in developing leadership and business skills
entry.summary: Women farmers are vital to Canada’s agriculture sector and rural communities. Supporting women farmers in developing their business and leadership skills helps strengthen the sector and promote farming as a career for women. This support is especially timely as 2026 has been proclaimed the International Year of Women Farmers by the United Nations.

entry.title: Government of Canada provides an update the 2026 wildfire season – October update
entry.summary: Wildfire seasons are now longer, more complex and more challenging than in the past, and 2026 was no exception. After a slower than average start to the season, wildfire activity, driven by periods of prolonged heat, drought and low humidity, became significant in several regions across the country. Northwestern Ontario and Southern British Columbia were particularly affected, experiencing sustained wildfire activity that threatened communities and critical infrastructure. Wildfire activity was also extremely intense in the Northwest Territories, which accounted for over one third of the total area burned in Canada in 2026.

entry.title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in St. Thomas
entry.summary: Today, the Governments of Canada and Ontario announced that the City of St. Thomas is receiving up to $19.6 million through the Development Charge Reduction Program (DCRP) in recognition of its commitment to reduce development charges by 30 per cent for single-detached homes and multi-unit housing, and 50 per cent for remaining unit types from March 30, 2026 to March 31, 2029.

entry.title: Building Canada Strong: Government of Canada and Atlantic Provinces invest $300 million through the Atlantic Fisheries Fund to help Atlantic seafood reach new markets
entry.summary: Today, the Minister of Fisheries, the Honourable Joanne Thompson, announced the renewal of the Atlantic Fisheries Fund (AFF) for a further five years. Minister Thompson was joined by the Honourable Kent Smith, Minister of Fisheries and Aquaculture for Nova Scotia; the Honourable Pat Finnigan, Minister of Agriculture, Aquaculture and Fisheries for New Brunswick; the Honourable Ernie Hudson, Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism for Prince Edward Island; and the Honourable Loyola O’Driscoll, Minister of Fisheries and Aquaculture for Newfoundland and Labrador.

entry.title: Government of Canada invests in Youth Gang Prevention in Manitoba and Alberta
entry.summary: Today, the Honourable Gary Anandasangaree, Minister of Public Safety, announced $1.6 million in federal funding to the Joy Smith Foundation through the Youth Gang Prevention Fund (YGPF) to support a project that will help prevent violence, gang involvement and criminal activity among at-risk and incarcerated youth aged 12 to 30 in Manitoba and Alberta.

entry.title: Government of Canada invests in stronger air connectivity in Norman Wells and Fort Simpson
entry.summary: Canadians, travellers, tourists and businesses count every day on local and regional airports. These vital hubs help move people and goods, strengthen supply chains, and link communities across our vast country from coast to coast to coast.

entry.title: Canada advances Wind West to bring major new clean power to Atlantic Canada
entry.summary: Today’s announcement builds on the Atlantic Economic Panel’s call to develop the region’s energy resources and strengthen electricity connections between provinces. Alongside the historic new Churchill Falls agreement, which represented the largest clean energy investment in North American history, it demonstrates the federal government’s commitment to unlocking Atlantic Canada’s potential as a clean energy superpower. Building out new clean electricity will bring economic prosperity, energy security, thousands of job opportunities, and a cleaner future to Canadians on the east coast and beyond.
